chapter: Working with Duke and final reflections
title: Closing: playing 'Come Sunday' and Whaley's own tune
summary: Hinton asks Whaley to try Count Basie's old electric piano; he sings 'Come Sunday' and his own 'I'd Do Almost Anything for You'.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: What the blues is, and why every jazz player needs it

blocks.x: Tom, I've got an old Licker piano over here that used to belong to Count Basie, who was my neighbor and when he moved, I kept it -- and I'm gonna turn it on, and I just want you, as a closing thing, just to touch it and play a little something for me so I can have it on the tape.
What shall I play?
No, I'll leave that up to you, but I just want you to do it so that these young people ...
Shall I play 'Come Sunday'?
Yeah, well, we'll talk about that later. Just let me cut this off now.
What'll I play first?

Tom, we're sitting here with you, just to close out our tape -- I got this old piano here that belonged to Count Basie, one of them electric pianos, and it's sitting here in the house, and I just thought I would ask you to play the tune that you conducted for Joe Williams to sing at the White House for Duke Ellington's 70th birthday party -- what was the name of that?
'Come Sunday.'
'Come Sunday' -- will you play a little taste of that for us?
(MR. WHALEY SINGS)
Oh, that was just beautiful. Thank you, Tom -- I didn't know you were going to sing it, too.
This is my number. ("In Love's Garden You Are My Bouquet.")

That's beautiful, Tom. Now just play me a little portion just for the record, see, a number which you hold claim to -- one of the most famous numbers that Claude Hopkins uses as his theme song, which you wrote and didn't get credit for.
What's the name of this?

'I'd do almost anything for you -- I would would swim the ocean line,/cross the Great Divide, I would do almost anything for you! In my heart, there's ecstasy as long as I have you, I'd do almost anything for you.'
(SINGING)
Beautiful. Okay, Tom. We got room for you to play it, so play it right on out to the end.
Thank you, Tom. That's beautiful. This is the most rewarding thing for me.
(CUT)
(END OF PROCEEDINGS AS RECORDED)
